summary.value: The Night-Elf court of ceremony, diplomacy, and performance, ruled by a young Prince trained in all three — and not in war. His mirrored combat style exists because he learns to fight by copying the protagonist: the hero is literally his first teacher of violence. The court's skeleton-knight honor guard is loaned from the Reliquary Crypt, an old gesture of friendship between the realms.

sharedOpinions.reason: He mistook a court of dancers for a war council, and now our Prince parries with the hero's own stolen forms. We grieve what our ruler is learning.
Their knights stand our ceremonies with us, and their King taught our Prince that remembrance is a ruler's first duty.
The Warden's treaties include our oldest signatures. If anyone can make the outsider read them, it is the keeper of those records.

examples.value: A mirror shows you exactly what you bring into the room.
Ceremony is just memory performed standing up.

meaning.value: The Prince's gift for learning any art by copying a master. It was meant for dance and oratory; the hero gave it nothing else to copy.
The skeleton-knight honor guard sent by the Reliquary Crypt for the court's great ceremonies — a standing loan between friends, never a tribute.

customs.value: Guests are received with a short performed welcome — a verse, a step, a phrase in the guest's own tongue. Refusing to watch it is the court's one true insult.
Every dispute opens with a full restating of the other side's position, performed to their satisfaction, before any answer is given.

taboos.value: Never teach a young ruler violence before ceremony. The court blames itself for letting the hero be the Prince's first fencing master.
Never mock another realm's ceremonies. Diplomacy has kept ten realms at peace for ten thousand years; the court treats that record as sacred.
